idiom_name: event loop plus libuv thread pool, extended with worker_threads for CPU-bound work
implementation_notes: The host already runs the asynchronous layer: the event loop demultiplexes while libuv's thread pool moves file, DNS, zlib and crypto work off it, so the classic POSA2 structure is implicit rather than built. When the synchronous layer is application code, it is realised with worker_threads: a small pool of Worker instances receives jobs through postMessage or a SharedArrayBuffer ring and returns results as messages, with the worker's message port acting as the queueing layer. The cost model differs from thread pools: workers are separate isolates with their own heaps, so hand-offs copy or transfer data instead of sharing it.
pitfalls: A synchronous call on the event loop (readFileSync, a long regex, pbkdf2Sync) stalls every connection: the asynchronous layer must never block.
Worker threads are not free - each has its own isolate and heap, and large payloads are copied or transferred; batch work and measure before adding workers.
postMessage has no back-pressure signal of its own; bound the in-flight jobs per worker or the message queues grow without limit.
